clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male presented with acute painless progressive bilateral vision loss over five days; ophthalmology exam revealed bilateral vitritis with white tufts and globular opacities suggestive of posterior uveitis consistent with syphilis. Risk factors included recent alopecia and sexual history. On admission, rapid plasmin reagin (RPR) test was positive, raising suspicion for ocular syphilis. Treatment with a 14-day course of IV penicillin G was initiated in the emergency department. No confirmatory treponemal antibody test results or RPR quantitative titers were documented, nor was follow-up clinical response or ophthalmologic findings reported.
